verses.1: And Jehizkiah was sent over all of Israel and Judah. He also wrote letters to the people of Ephraim and Manasseh, telling them to come to Jerusalem to celebrate Passover in honor of Jehovah, the God of Israel.
verses.2: The king, his ministers, and all the people in Jerusalem were commanded to observe Passover in the second month.
verses.3: For they could not do it at that time, because the priests were not sanctified yet, and the people did not gather in Jerusalem.
verses.4: And it was shown to the king and to all the people.
verses.5: And they set forth to spread the word throughout all of Israel, from Shevah to Dan, so that people might celebrate Passover in Jerusalem. For they did not do it as it was written.
verses.6: And the prophets went out, under the command of the king and his officials, throughout all of Israel and Judah. They did this as commanded by the king: “Children of Israel, return to Jehovah, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Return to your rightful place among you, from among the kings of Assyria.”
verses.7: And do not be like your ancestors and their gods, who were given to worshiping those idols. They were given to them by the God of their ancestors, just as you see now.
verses.8: Now, do not be troubled by your pains. Let go of your fears and come before Jehovah’s temple. Serve Jehovah, your God, and let His grace be restored among you.
verses.9: For when you return to Jehovah, your brothers and children will have mercy upon you before they die. And when you return to this land, as Hanun said, may Jehovah, your God, show you mercy. He will not take away your faces if you return to Him.
verses.10: And they traveled from one city to another across the land of Ephraim. They went from Menashe to Zbulun. They mocked and laughed at them.
verses.11: But the people of Ashur, Manaas, and Zebulun were subdued, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.12: Also in Judah, the hand of God would be with them, so that they could have one heart and carry out the commands of the king and the priests regarding the words of Jehovah.
verses.13: And Jerusalem gathered a large crowd to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles in the second month. There was a very large crowd there.
verses.14: And they stood up and removed all the idols that were in Jerusalem. They also removed all the altars, and threw them into the Kedron River.
verses.15: And they sacrificed Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites were sanctified. They brought offerings to the house of Jehovah.
verses.16: And they stood in their places, as commanded by Moses, the servant of God. The priests poured the blood from the hands of the Levites.
verses.17: For there are many who have not been sanctified, and those who slaughter the Passover animals for all purposes are not pure enough to be used for Jehovah’s service.
verses.18: For the people became too proud and arrogant. Zebulun and Naftali did not become pure, because they ate the Passover without following the laws of God’s commandments. Therefore, Jehizkia prayed for them, saying, “May the Lord do what is good for them.”
verses.19: His whole heart is prepared for serving the Lord, Jehovah, the God of his ancestors. It isn’t done out of a sense of holiness or purity.
verses.20: And Jehovah heard Elishama, and he healed the people.
verses.21: And the Israelites who were living in Jerusalem celebrated the Festival of Tabernacles for seven days, with great joy and praise to the Lord. It was a day of celebration for the people and the priests, all in honor of the Lord.
verses.22: And Jehizkiah spoke to the hearts of all those wise men who had a good understanding of God. They ate the offerings that were given for seven days, offering sacrifices of peace offerings and worshiping God, their ancestors’ God.
verses.23: And all the people decided to spend seven more days doing nothing. So they spent seven days in joy.
verses.24: For Jehoshua, king of Judah, he brought to the people ten thousand sheep and seven thousand lambs. The priests also brought to the people ten thousand sheep and twelve thousand lambs. They sanctified these animals as offerings for the priests.
verses.25: And all the people of Judah, the priests, the Levites, and all those who came from Israel, as well as the foreigners who came from the land of Israel, and those who lived in Judah, were very happy.
verses.26: There was great joy in Jerusalem, because since the time of Solomon son of David, king of Israel, there had never been such joy in Jerusalem before.
verses.27: And the priests stood up and blessed the people. Their voices were heard, and their prayers were accepted by God.
